acquisition_matrix.acquisition_method_verdict: Lane #1 (act0_real_text_surface_capture_v1.dart / screen_review_fast_v1.sh) confirmed as primary evidence tier, consistent with the strategy checkpoint. No new acquisition method was introduced beyond the authorized reduced-motion modifier.

reduced_motion.implementation: tools/act0_real_text_surface_capture_v1.dart accepts an optional 3rd CLI arg 'reduced_motion'; all 4 internal test-source generators set WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.accessibilityFeaturesTestValue = FakeAccessibilityFeatures(disableAnimations: true) when set. Manifest gains a 'motion_mode' field ('normal'|'reduced'). Output packet directory gets a '_reduced_motion' suffix so normal and reduced captures do not collide.
reduced_motion.result: All three pass. Reduced-motion capture surfaced one new (expected) duplicate-hash pair in sharky_evidence (improve|milestone) caused by removing an incidental animation-phase difference between two states that already share the same provisional fallback asset; added to the tool's intentional_same_state_allowlist with an explicit reason. Not a new product defect -- confirms the already-tracked EXTERNAL_ASSET_INPUT_REQUIRED Sharky-art gap more precisely than normal-motion capture did.

s3_disposition.reproduction: dart run tools/act0_real_text_surface_capture_v1.dart presentation_closure compact reproduced the exact reported mismatch at the fresh Wave V1 baseline: Expected Rect.fromLTRB(45.4,46.0,356.6,586.2) vs Actual Rect.fromLTRB(83.5,46.0,318.5,454.0), identical to the strategy checkpoint's report at the prior baseline.
s3_disposition.root_cause: The failing assertion (long_copy_repair_feedback: expect(table, tableRectForCycle)) requires the practice table to be byte-identical in position and size between the four-option decision state and the long-copy repair-feedback state. That assertion was added in commit 8b83d4ac (2026-07-16). Nine days later, commit 40cae60b (2026-07-25, "fix(learning): close native feedback parity") intentionally introduced shared-active-runner-allocation logic that lets the table shrink -- centered on its horizontal midpoint, anchored at its top -- to grant a long-copy repair-feedback surface its measured lower-slot demand, fixing a real occlusion bug where the table could cover the repair heading. The exact-equality assertion was never updated to match. The strict 'table never moves' contract that assertion assumed only actually applies to a different, unused code path (_TaskOwnedStablePracticePresentationV1, explicitly gated on !usesSharedActiveRunnerAllocation).
s3_disposition.owner_family: Capture-tool fixture only (tools/act0_real_text_surface_capture_v1.dart). No lib/ui_v2/act0_shell product code was changed -- the product's shared-allocation table-shrink behavior is confirmed intentional and correct.
s3_disposition.fix: Replaced the exact-rect-equality assertion with the real invariant the current design guarantees: table.top unchanged, table.center.dx unchanged (within 0.5px), width/height monotonically non-increasing. Also lengthened the long-copy repair-feedback fixture's repairReasonLine (previously ~90 characters, insufficient under the current generously-sized lower dock to ever force a scroll) so the surface's own named scenario -- and its scrollable-overflow assertion -- is genuinely exercised again.
s3_disposition.verification: presentation_closure lane passes at compact/tall_phone/large_phone after the fix. Full ./tools/release_gate_world1.sh passes (97 tests, fast loop, gate green).
s3_disposition.forbidden_scope_respected: No composition redesign, no shared-shell work, no Sharky assets, no Modern Table changes. Fix is confined to the capture tool's own fixture assertions and fixture text.

simulator_parity.tooling_used: tools/capture_act0_screens_v1.sh, unmodified in the repository (only surfaces: home|learn|practice|review|profile). Local one-time uncommitted device-name substitution was required: the script hardcodes 'iPhone 17', which is not an available simulator runtime on this machine; iPhone 16 Pro (already booted) was substituted for the session and the temporary copy was deleted afterward -- no committed tooling change.
states_not_reachable: session summary/milestone or 1.4x accessibility state -- this simpler simulator script does not expose those surfaces
simulator_parity.comparison_result: For home/learn/review: correct screen/state identity, visible real text, correct fonts/asset loading, respected safe area, matching major geometry and CTA placement, correct scrollability, reachable bottom content, and no unexpected platform chrome, consistent with lane #1's equivalent captures.
simulator_parity.disposition_reason: Lane #1 is confirmed reliable for composition/text/CTA/safe-area claims on every risk class actually reachable by the existing simulator tooling. The feedback/repair and milestone/accessibility risk classes were not independently spot-checked on a real device this wave because the existing capture_act0_screens_v1.sh does not expose those surfaces -- a tooling gap, not a parity failure. Future evidence rules should not claim device-verified parity for those two states specifically until the simulator script (or a successor) can reach them.

symptom_ledger.learner_visible_impact: Screen reads as unfinished/empty on a learning app; the zero-content and onboarding-entry branches leave 30-40% of the compact viewport blank below the last element.
symptom_ledger.root_cause_cluster: Weak vertical-allocation grammar for empty/low-content states -- no shared minimum-fill or centering contract; each screen composes its own vertical stack.
symptom_ledger.causal_owner: lib/ui_v2/act0_shell composition layer -- specifically the review zero-state branch and the onboarding/welcome template branch (two distinct owner families, not one).
symptom_ledger.confidence: high -- directly observed in fresh commit-pinned lane-#1 captures this wave, confirming the strategy checkpoint's original review_empty finding and adding one new owner family (onboarding).
symptom_ledger.recommended_repair_model: Model 3 (narrow vertical-allocation grammar: min-fill or center-with-secondary-element rule), applied to exactly these two owner families. Two independently-owned families is below the 3+ threshold the strategy set for the Model 1 shared-shell fallback.
